newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's ruling PRI loses congressional majority.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's ruling PRI loses congressional majority.

text.p: Mexico's ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) lost its absolute majority in the lower house of Congress in midterm elections, official results showed on Thursday.
The PRI, which has ruled Mexico since 1929, fell short of the minimum 167 of 300 directly elected seats in the lower house needed to clinch a majority, the results indicated.

With Sunday's ballots for 294 of 300 directly elected seats counted, the PRI had won 159 seats against 69 for the leftist Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) and 65 for the conservative National Action Party (PAN).

Under Mexico's complicated electoral law, the PRI needed at least 167 of the directly elected seats and 42.2 percent of the national vote to win an outright majority in the 500 seat body -- something it has had since the party was founded in the aftermath of the 1910-17 Mexican Revolution.
"There is no way the PRI can have an absolute majority in the lower house," a high-ranking official of Mexico's Federal Electoral Institute (IFE), told Reuters.

The remaining 200 seats in the lower house were to be alloted according to each party's share of the overall vote, election officials said. The allotment system would have been slightly different were the PRI guaranteed a majority.
After finishing the vote count in all but three Mexican states, IFE said the PRI had won 38.43 percent of the ballots, followed by 28.98 percent for the PAN and 25.71 percent for the PRD.

If current trends hold, the PRI would be about seven or eight seats short of a majority in the lower house, which up to now has simply rubber-stamped initiatives from the country's powerful president, according to political analysts.
The election marked a watershed change for a country dominated by a single party for seven decades and gave the opposition its first serious voice in government since 1929.
The PRI was also hit hard by its loss in the first-ever election for Mexico City mayor, which leftist and PRI-critic Cuauhtemoc Cardenas won easily.

The northern state of Sonora, the southern state of Tabasco and the central state of Puebla were not included in the percentage tally on Thursday because the six remaining directly elected seats to be counted were from districts in those states.
"Those districts are being contested in some way or other by one of the parties and their results will not be known for some time," said Berta Sanchez, a spokeswoman for the IFE.

The three states together accounted for about 1.85 million votes of the 29.32 million cast during the election, officials said. The PRI's support was running at about 46 percent in Puebla, 55 percent in Tabasco and 36 percent in Sonora.
IFE officials said they would complete the vote count in the remaining districts later on Thursday or early on Friday, but may not release the results until Sunday.
